Blocking histamine-driven acid secretion

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A 41-year-old woman begins famotidine for nocturnal acid-related symptoms. In a parallel laboratory study, the same medicine reduces histamine-stimulated signaling in isolated gastric parietal cells without directly inactivating the proton pump. Which receptor is directly blocked to produce this effect?

  1. Histamine H2 receptor
  2. Histamine H1 receptor
  3. Muscarinic M3 receptor
  4. Gastrin CCK-B receptor
  5. Serotonin 5-HT3 receptor
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Histamine H2 receptor

H2 antagonism reduces histamine-stimulated parietal-cell acid secretion.

Understanding the options

Histamine H2 receptor
H2 antagonism reduces histamine-stimulated parietal-cell acid secretion.
Histamine H1 receptor
H1 receptors mediate many allergic and vestibular effects.
Muscarinic M3 receptor
M3 receptors mediate cholinergic stimulation.
Gastrin CCK-B receptor
CCK-B receptors mediate gastrin signaling.
Serotonin 5-HT3 receptor
5-HT3 receptors are involved in emetic signaling.
